NicolasStigler opened PR #15072 from NicolasStigler:fix/aarch64-bti-indirect-targets to bytecodealliance:main:

Fixes #14938

Why

With BTI and pointer authentication enabled on AArch64, several indirect control-flow paths could trap with an illegal instruction. The affected cases include br_table defaults, exception-handler targets, indirect tail calls, and tail-convention prologues using paciaz/pacibz.

What changed

  • Mark br_table defaults and exception-handler targets as indirect branch targets so they receive bti j.
  • Emit bti c before paciaz/pacibz where needed.
  • Route indirect tail calls through x16 before branching.
  • Add and update AArch64 filetests and runtime configurations for BTI and pointer authentication.

Testing

  • cargo +1.97.0 fmt --all -- --check
  • cargo +1.97.0 clippy -p cranelift-codegen --all-targets
  • cargo +1.97.0 test -p cranelift-codegen
  • cargo +1.97.0 test -p cranelift-filetests
  • cargo +1.97.0 test -p cranelift-tools --test filetests
  • cargo +1.97.0 test -p cranelift-tools --test logged-filetests
  • AArch64 Wasmtime WAST reproducers under QEMU with BTI and pointer-authentication enabled

Thanks! A few thoughts below but overall looks good.

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

Can we do this only when PAC/BTI is enabled? I don't want to pessimize the case when it's not (e.g. default aarch64 Linux).

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

Let's make a note that this is the spill-temp register, which by Cranelift convention we are allowed to use as a scratch register within one VCode inst, so this is safe.
